podcast.title: Banksy's Motivation for Think Tank (2003) Artwork
podcast.body: Banksy reportedly stated that he undertook the Think Tank artwork partly for the money, explaining that while painting walls could make one famous, it did not provide a living. "decía que lo hizo por la cia parte del dinero porque pintaron las calles de cabía pero no te ha de comer."

srcs.episode: Blur - Think Tank y su dificil grabación.

podcast.title: Think Tank (2003) Album Cover
podcast.body: The famous cover art for Blur's album Think Tank was created directly by Banksy, not merely inspired by his style, for which he received a significant payment. "la famosa portada del Cintan la hizo Basky pero el Basky me verdad no está inspirado en Basky sino que es Basky quien hizo esta portada y ganó bastante dinero a cien gra."

srcs.episode: Blur - Think Tank y su dificil grabación.

podcast.title: Think Tank (2003) Cover and Back Cover Artwork Payment
podcast.body: Banksy was paid a substantial amount for designing both the front and back covers of Blur's Think Tank, which subsequently became an iconic image in music history. "Le pagaron mucha dinero por hacer lo que fue la portada del Cintan y la contraportada del Cintan y la verdad es que la portaba y el diés un icono de la historia de la música."

srcs.episode: Blur - Think Tank y su dificil grabación.

podcast.title: Demanding Graham Coxon's Departure
podcast.body: Manayerti, Blur's manager, ultimately instructed Graham Coxon to leave the group during the Think Tank sessions due to his disruptive behavior, a decision the rest of the band supported as the situation had become impossible. "el manayer acabó diciendo a la grabación cocción que se fuese de el grupo y se marcha si lo dejase trabajar tranquilos, a lo que el resto del grupo accedió porque la situación era rádia en imposibilidad."

podcast.title: Famous Anonymous Graffiti Artist
podcast.body: Banksy is a famous graffiti artist whose work sells for millions of dollars, yet his identity remains unknown. "Banksy, the famous graffiti artist, who's worked cell for millions of dollars. Nobody knows who Banksy is."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Generational Symbol
podcast.body: Banksy is acknowledged not only as the most important graffitero today but also as a significant generational symbol, having emerged from The Wild Bunch collective. "pero también tenemos al increíble Bansky, el gran citaro más importante que tenemos en día y un símbolo generacional."

srcs.episode: Massive Attack y El Origen del Trip Hop en Bristol.

podcast.title: Graffitero Member of The Wild Bunch
podcast.body: Banksy, described as possibly the most important graffitero in history after Keith Haring, was one of the members of The Wild Bunch during the 1980s. He was a graffitero alongside Robert "3D" Del Naja in that group. "otro de los grafiteros que estaba con él en ese grupo es el famoso Bansky."

podcast.body: Fatboy Slim is mentioned as the producer of 'Syntac', which is used as a reference point to illustrate Damon Albarn's heavy influence in electronic music. "farboy y rin es el productor de Cintac."

podcast.title: Role in Calming Blur Tensions
podcast.body: Manayerti, described as a great friend of the group Blur, helped to calm the tense initial reunion of the band members during the early stages of recording Think Tank. "gracias a Manayerti, siempre ha sido un gran amigo del grupo, se siguió un poco solentada."

podcast.title: Suspected Identities
podcast.body: Some speculate that Banksy might be 3D (Robert Del Naja) from the group Massive Attack, or Jamie Hewlett, who collaborates with Damon Albarn on Gorillaz. Another theory suggests he is Robin Gunningham, an artist from Bristol who once called himself Robin Banks, potentially evolving into Banksy. "Although some suspect that he might be 3D, otherwise known as Robert Naja in the group Massive Attack. Or maybe Banksy is actually Jamie Hewitt, the guy who works with Damon Albard and Gorillas. Or it might be a guy named Robin Gunningham, an artist from Bristol who started calling himself Robin Banks, which may have eventually become Banksy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
